summary.title: How to be a -10x Engineer
summary.one_liner: A satirical checklist of anti-patterns (wasted hours, pointless meetings, bloated cloud costs, bad architecture) that show how an engineer could destroy a team's productivity, read as a list of what not to do.
keywords: how not to be a good engineer
takeaways: Satirical list of behaviours that multiply wasted engineering hours, framed as the opposite of a 10x engineer.
Anti-patterns covered include changing requirements late, slow builds and tests, mocked-out tests, and unnecessary deployment environments.
Cultural anti-patterns include hoarding decisions, endless meetings, skipping documentation, and protecting bad engineers.
Useful as a quick self-check of common team-level pitfalls, delivered with humour.
summary.summary: This short satirical essay lists strategies for becoming a "-10x engineer" by wasting hundreds of engineering hours. Each item pairs a bad behaviour with its cost, covering project management (shifting requirements, pointless rituals), tooling (slow builds, undocumented scripts), testing (mocked tests that check nothing), architecture, deployment, cloud spending, documentation, and hiring. The page is a list of anti-patterns rather than a tutorial, with no code or tools. It is intended as humour, but the items map onto real engineering problems.
